results.prompt: Brew me a Premodern deck built around Waterfront Bouncer and Squee, Goblin Nabob.
results.text:
This is a mono-blue Merfolk deck that runs Squee as discard fodder and never casts it. Squee comes back to your hand from the graveyard every upkeep, so each turn you can discard it to pay for Waterfront Bouncer ({U}, tap, discard a card: return target creature to its owner's hand) and get it back next turn. Repeated every turn, Bouncer sends the opponent's best creature back to their hand without costing you a card.

**How it wins:**
1. Play Tidal Warrior on turn 1 and Lord of Atlantis on turn 2. The Lord gives your other Merfolk +1/+1 and islandwalk, so they can't be blocked by a player with an Island. Tidal Warrior can turn one of their lands into an Island for the turn, so this works against non-blue decks too.
2. From turn 3, Bouncer returns their best blocker or threat every turn, paid for with Squee.
3. Winter Orb lets each player untap only one land per turn, so they can't replay what you bounced.
4. Counterspell, Daze, Gush, Foil, Thwart and Stifle protect the board while unblockable 2/2s close the game around turn 7.

**Directions I considered:**
- **Mono-blue Merfolk with Squee as fodder (chosen).** Real decks already pair these two cards: 4 of the 6 recent Merfolk lists that run Bouncer also run Squee. Staying mono-blue keeps the free spells (Daze, Gush, Foil, Thwart) that need Islands.
- **Blue-red tempo** that actually casts Squee, with Grim Lavamancer and burn. It would cost those free spells and gain only a 1/1 body.
- **Blue-green Madness** with Wild Mongrel and Basking Rootwalla. It spreads the deck's discards across too many payoffs, so Bouncer stops being the focus.

**Things to know:**
- The deck checker warns that there are no red sources for Squee. That's intentional, since Squee is never cast. With 3 copies you usually have one, and every copy in your graveyard returns each upkeep.
- Merfolk Looter (draw a card, then discard) and Foil (counter a spell by discarding an Island and another card) also use Squee as the discard.
- The land base copies the proven Merfolk mana: 18 lands, 16 blue sources.
- **Honest odds:** without counting the cantrips, you have Bouncer plus either Squee or Looter by turn 4 in about 38% of games. Bouncer alone shows up by turn 4 about 53% of the time. Looter, Gush and Portent help you dig for the pieces.
- The checker found that a game draws every card in the full win line by turn 7 only about 2% of the time. The line doesn't need every card, though: Bouncer, Squee and a Lord are enough to take over.

The 15-card sideboard covers the top decks: Annul against Enchantress, Blue Elemental Blast and Hydroblast against Sligh and Goblins, Tormod's Crypt against Hermit Druid and Replenish, and Submerge against green decks.

--- After playtest ---
I fixed all three problems and resubmitted the deck. It was accepted as a legal 60-card list.

**1. Squee dead copies (fixed, partly my way).** Squee goes from 3 to 2, and I added 1 Standstill. I kept 2 Squees instead of 1 because the deck still has to draw Squee before it can discard it. Also, every copy in the graveyard comes back each upkeep, so two copies can pay for Bouncer and Masticore in the same turn. The deck still has no red sources, so Squee is never cast; the deck checker flags this as a warning and that's intentional.

**2. Not enough real threats (fixed differently).** I cut both Stifles. Sea Drake isn't legal in Premodern, so instead I added **2 Masticore**:
- It's a 4/4 that can pay {2} to deal 1 damage to a creature or to regenerate, so it can attack through lock pieces and clear small blockers.
- Its upkeep cost is "discard a card or sacrifice it." Squee returns to hand in that same upkeep and can be the discard, so Masticore stays at almost no card cost.

That makes Squee a bigger part of the deck rather than a smaller one. I passed on Rishadan Port because it adds no damage. The new Standstill also gives card advantage against slow decks.

**3. Too much Daze, and Thwart hurts our own mana (fixed).** I cut Thwart and 1 Daze, and added a 3rd Foil and 1 Mana Leak. Foil can be paid for by discarding an Island and Squee. Mana Leak makes the opponent pay {3} instead of Daze's {1}, which matters more against mana-heavy decks.

**Weak spots that remain:**
- Masticore costs 4, and our own Winter Orb makes that harder, so I kept it at 2 copies.
- The deck runs only 18 lands. The checker suggests about 22, so mana could be tight.
- The checker says that by turn 6, about 0.1% of games have drawn every card in the win line. That's because the list requires all seven cards together, and the deck usually wins with only some of them. Still, it's no evidence that the deck is fast.

**Final list:** 4 Lord of Atlantis, 4 Waterfront Bouncer, 4 Merfolk Looter, 4 Tidal Warrior, 2 Squee, 2 Masticore, 4 Counterspell, 3 Daze, 4 Gush, 3 Foil, 1 Mana Leak, 3 Winter Orb, 1 Standstill, 2 Portent, 1 Chain of Vapor, and 18 lands. The sideboard is unchanged.

winLine.does: Turn 1 one-drop; taps to turn an opponent's land into an Island so islandwalk works against non-blue decks
Turn 2: other Merfolk get +1/+1 and islandwalk, making Bouncer, Looter and Warrior unblockable 2/2 attackers
Turn 3: pays {U} and discards Squee to bounce the opponent's best creature or blocker each turn
Never cast; discarded to Bouncer, Looter, Foil or Masticore, then returns to hand every upkeep so each discard costs no real card
4/4 clock whose upkeep discard is paid by Squee returning in the same upkeep; {2} pings clear small blockers

playtest.game:
Keep: 5 lands plus Counterspell and Daze is fine against Enchantress. The alternative 7 has one land and would also cost a card. Me 20, Opp 20.
T1: Island, pass. Opp: Forest, Wild Growth; I hold Daze for something that matters.
T2: draw Island. Play Polluted Delta and pass with Counterspell up. Opp casts Argothian Enchantress; I crack Delta (19 life) and Counterspell it.
T3: draw Merfolk Looter. Play Island, cast Looter, hold Daze. Opp has 4 mana and casts Enchantress's Presence with 1 spare, so I don't Daze. Opp plays Wild Growth and draws off Presence.
T4: draw Gush. Loot away Flooded Strand (excess land) and keep Island in hand. Looter attacks: Opp 19. Opp plays Exploration, then Elephant Grass; I Daze the Grass but Opp pays (Wild Growth mana).
T5: draw Waterfront Bouncer and cast it. Pay Grass for Looter to attack: Opp 18. Opp plays Serra's Sanctum and Sterling Grove, drawing 2. I Wasteland the Sanctum at end of turn.
T6: draw Island. Loot. Gush (return 2 Islands) at Opp end step and draw into lands. Opp casts Seal of Cleansing and Mirri's Guile, sculpting freely. My board is a 1/1 Looter and a 1/1 Bouncer, and Bouncer has no creature targets.
T7: draw Squee, uncastable with no red source. It is only Bouncer fodder, and there is nothing to bounce. Opp casts Parallax Wave; I have no counter left in hand.
T8: draw Flooded Strand (fetch: 18 life). Opp resolves Opalescence through my empty hand. Its enchantments are now creatures; Grass and Wave blank my attacks.
T9: draw Gush. Bouncer discards Squee to bounce an animated enchantment, but Presence and Exploration let Opp replay it and draw. Opp attacks with 4-5 animated enchantments. Me 18 -> 7.
T10: Squee returns to hand; I bounce again, but I'm fading 1-for-0 against a card engine. Opp swings for lethal. Loss.

problems.problem: Squee, Goblin Nabob can never be cast: the deck has zero red sources, and neither Flooded Strand nor Polluted Delta can fetch a Mountain. It only works as discard fodder for Waterfront Bouncer, Merfolk Looter or Foil. Drawn without Bouncer it is a blank. Being legendary and self-returning, the extra copies are redundant: one Squee in the graveyard already recurs every upkeep. Three copies is roughly two dead cards per game.
problems.fix: Cut Squee from 3 to 1 and add 2 Standstill. Standstill is a card-advantage threat that fits the Winter Orb tempo plan and is strong against durdly decks like Enchantress.

problems.problem: Threat density is too low and the threats are tiny. Outside Lord of Atlantis, every creature is a 1/1 or 1/2 utility dork. Waterfront Bouncer and Merfolk Looter are engines, not clocks. With no Lord drawn, the deck dealt 2 damage in 10 turns while Elephant Grass and Parallax Wave walled it off. Against creature-light decks, the Bouncer half of the theme is blank.
problems.fix: Cut 2 Stifle and add 2 Rishadan Port, or a real body such as Sea Drake. Give the deck threats that pressure through lock pieces rather than more narrow interaction.

problems.problem: The counter suite is too reliant on Daze, which is soft and gets paid for easily by mana-rich decks (Wild Growth, Exploration). Meanwhile Gush and Thwart actively bounce your own lands and stunt mana in a deck already short on threats. In this game Counterspell was the only counter that actually stopped a key card.
problems.fix: Cut Thwart and 1 Daze and add a 3rd Foil plus 1 Force Spike, or Mana Leak. Foil can pitch Squee, which also ties the fodder theme together.

toolCalls.name: submit_deck
rejected: Waterfront Bouncer needs "Free discard fodder that comes back every upkeep", and the deck has 2 copies of the cards that provide it (Squee, Goblin Nabob). A build-around's enablers are usually 6+ copies: add some, or resubmit with needsReason saying why 2 is enough here.

results.prompt: Brew me a mono-blue Premodern deck built around Waterfront Bouncer and Gilded Drake.
results.text:
I built a mono-blue tempo deck on mono-blue Merfolk's shell, and submit_deck accepted it as a brew.

**The plan:** Gilded Drake swaps itself for the opponent's best creature on turn 2. Then Waterfront Bouncer (pay U, tap, discard a card) returns the Drake from their side to your hand, so you can cast it again and take a second creature. The first stolen creature stays yours for good. Lord of Atlantis turns your 1/1 Merfolk into 2/2 islandwalkers, and the counterspells (Counterspell, Daze, Foil, Stifle) protect the board you've taken.

**Directions I considered:**
1. **Merfolk tempo with a counterspell package** (chosen). Bouncer is already in 67% of real Merfolk lists, and Bouncer is a Merfolk itself, so it gets the Lord bonus. I borrowed the counterspells from Stiflenought, a top deck right now.
2. **A slow control deck with Winter Orb (which stops lands from untapping) and creatures that do something when they enter.** I dropped it because Bouncer needs blue mana every turn and recasting the Drake needs mana too, which fights Winter Orb.
3. **Stiflenought with Drake and Bouncer in place of Phyrexian Dreadnought.** I dropped it because it has too few creatures for Bouncer to matter.

I picked option 1 because the current field is full of creatures worth stealing twice: Terravore, Nimble Mongoose, Grim Lavamancer, Argothian Enchantress, Goblins.

**Choices in the build:**
- **No mono-blue deck plays both cards:** the only real list running Drake and Bouncer together is a green Survival Madness deck.
- **Ways to return the Drake:** 4 Bouncer, 1 Chain of Vapor and 3 Man-o'-War. Man-o'-War also bounces blockers and is worth reusing with Bouncer.
- **Cards for Bouncer to discard:** Merfolk Looter, Gush and Opt keep cards coming, so you can usually pay for Bouncer with extra lands.
- **Odds:** you'll have both a Drake and a way to return it by turn 4 about 31% of the time. Each half still works alone: the Drake on its own is a steal, and Bouncer on its own bounces blockers.
- **17 Islands:** the checker suggested about 22 lands. I didn't follow that, because Gush, Daze and Foil can be cast by returning or discarding Islands instead of paying mana. Real Merfolk lists average 18 lands and Stiflenought averages 17.
- **No Winter Orb in the main deck:** every real Merfolk list plays it, but it slows down Bouncer and repeat Drakes. I moved 2 copies to the sideboard instead.
- **Winning line:** the full six-card line shows as 5.2% by turn 7, but that requires drawing every named card. It isn't the real win rate.

**Weakness:** The Drake has nothing to steal against creature-light decks like Enchantress and Replenish. If there's no opposing creature, you have to sacrifice it. Against those decks the Drake comes out after sideboarding.

**Sideboard (15):** 3 Annul, 3 Blue Elemental Blast, 2 Hydroblast, 2 Tormod's Crypt, 2 Submerge, 2 Winter Orb, 1 Powder Keg.

--- After playtest ---
I made two of the three fixes and turned down one. The deck was accepted with no warnings, and the plan is the same: steal a creature with Gilded Drake, send the Drake back to my hand with Waterfront Bouncer or Man-o'-War, steal again, then attack with Lord of Atlantis and the stolen creatures.

1. **Thin mana: fixed as suggested.** I cut 2 Stifle for 2 Islands, so the deck now runs 19 Islands. Daze and Gush return Islands to hand and Foil discards one, so the deck needs more lands to keep its land drops coming. The deck check still recommends about 22 lands, so 19 is a deliberate low count. It leans on the 4 Gush returning Islands to hand to make up the gap.
2. **Man-o'-War and Drake with no targets: kept in the main deck.** Man-o'-War is one of only three cards that can return the opponent's Drake to my hand, along with Waterfront Bouncer and Chain of Vapor, and most decks in the format do have creatures. Enchantress has almost none, so I fixed that matchup in the sideboard instead: 2 Boomerang (return any permanent to its owner's hand) replace 2 Winter Orb and come in against enchantment decks.
3. **Daze too soft: fixed differently.** I cut 2 Daze for 2 Mana Leak instead of 2 Annul. Mana Leak can counter any spell, while Annul only hits artifacts and enchantments, so it fits better in the main deck. The 3 Annul stay in the sideboard for Enchantress. Mana Leak can still be paid for late, but it doesn't cost me a land like Daze does. I kept 2 Daze for early tempo, and 4 Counterspell are still the hard counters.

The deck submitted with a turn-6 kill target. The tool rates assembling every card in the listed line by turn 6 at only about 1.4% of games. That number is a strict cap: the line I listed is a full sequence, and the tool doesn't simulate card draw. In practice, the real requirement is just Drake plus a way to send it back to my hand.

winLine.does: Turn 2: exchanges control with the opponent's best creature, leaving them a 3/3 flier.
Turn 3: U, tap, discard a card: returns the Drake the opponent controls to its owner's (your) hand; the stolen creature stays yours.
Alternate way to bounce the opponent-controlled Drake back to your hand on ETB.
Turn 4: recast to steal a second creature.
Gives merfolk +1/+1 and islandwalk to beat down alongside stolen creatures.
Turns an opposing land into an Island so islandwalk connects.
With Mana Leak, Daze and Foil, protects the stolen board while attacking.

playtest.game:
Mulligan: the first 7 has one Island and no creatures. The second 7 also has one Island; I keep 6 (Island, Daze, Daze, Waterfront Bouncer, Man-o'-War, Gilded Drake) and bottom Gush.
T1: Island. Opp: Forest, Utopia Sprawl.
T2: Draw Stifle, no second land, no play. Opp: Argothian Enchantress (shroud) with 1 mana spare, so Daze is pointless and I let it resolve.
T3: Draw Island, cast Waterfront Bouncer (2 lands). Opp: Wild Growth (draws), then Enchantress's Presence with mana open for Daze; it resolves. Opp draws 2.
T4: Draw Island (3 lands). Bouncer attacks (opp 18). Man-o'-War and Gilded Drake have no legal targets because Argothian has shroud. Opp: Ghostly Prison, drawing 2; they have spare mana, so Daze is weak.
T5: Draw Waterfront Bouncer and cast it. I pay 2 to attack with one Bouncer (opp 16). Opp: Serra's Sanctum and Sylvan Library; their hand is now huge.
T6: Draw Opt and cast it at end of turn. I pay the Prison tax for one attack (opp 14). Opp: Seal of Cleansing and Solitary Confinement (discarding to upkeep) with Sanctum mana; Daze is easily paid.
T7: Draw Daze. My attacks are pointless into Confinement, so I hold two Dazes and Stifle. Opp: Opalescence for 4, and my Dazes are paid through Sanctum. Their enchantments become creatures.
T8: Draw Tidal Warrior. Man-o'-War bounces an animated Presence (they recast it). Gilded Drake steals a 4/4 Ghostly Prison but gives them a 3/3 flyer. Opp swings with the animated board (me 13).
T9: Draw Lord of Atlantis; my Merfolk can't outrace the animated enchantments. Opp: Replenish rebuilds everything plus Parallax Wave; me 4.
T10: Opp swings for lethal. I lose.

problems.problem: The mana base is too thin for a deck whose free spells eat Islands. Seventeen Islands, plus 4 Daze and 4 Gush that bounce Islands and 2 Foil that discards one, means one-land hands and stumbles are common. Both opening sevens had a single Island, which forced a mulligan to 6, and I couldn't cast Daze and still develop. The Lord of Atlantis double-blue plus Bouncer activation curve also wants steady land drops.
problems.fix: Cut 2 Stifle (low-impact in most matchups) for 2 more Islands, going to 19.

problems.problem: Gilded Drake and Man-o'-War need opposing creatures, and the format's most-played deck barely has any. Argothian Enchantress has shroud, and the rest of the threats are enchantments. Drake had no target until Opalescence, then traded badly. Man-o'-War could only reset my own creatures. Waterfront Bouncer's activation was likewise blank.
problems.fix: Cut 3 Man-o'-War for 3 more Chain of Vapor-style flexible bounce (e.g. Boomerang), which can hit enchantments and lands as well as creatures.

problems.problem: Daze is a soft counter. Against a deck with Utopia Sprawl, Wild Growth and Serra's Sanctum it was paid every time after turn 2, yet it cost me a land when cast. The counter suite had no hard answer that stayed relevant once the opponent had spare mana.
problems.fix: Cut 2 Daze for 2 Annul-type cheap hard counters or a 5th-slot Counterspell substitute such as Mana Leak, keeping 2 Daze for early tempo.

toolCalls.name: submit_deck
rejected: Waterfront Bouncer needs "Lord bonus, since Bouncer is a Merfolk and becomes a 2/2 islandwalker", and the deck has 4 copies of the cards that provide it (Lord of Atlantis). A build-around's enablers are usually 6+ copies: add some, or resubmit with needsReason saying why 4 is enough here.
